context: In fractional knapsack, items are divisible. Comparing their values per unit of weight tells you more about which to take first than comparing the values of whole items.
description: The table on the left lists the five items by original item number, with fruit names taken from the icons. The fourth column is labeled “Unit value val[i-1] / wgt[i-1].” The values 5, 6, 5, 5.25, and 4.8 appear in the diagram itself. On the right, multiplying the weight taken, w, by the unit value gives the value added to the knapsack.

frames.explanation: For example, the apple's unit value is 50 ÷ 10 = 5. The relationship on the right is weight taken w × unit value val[i-1] / wgt[i-1] = value added to the knapsack. It applies to both whole items and fractions. The banana has the highest unit value in the table, followed by the pineapple.
frames.title: Value per unit of weight

summary: Unit value is an item's value divided by its weight. Taking a portion of weight w adds w times the item's unit value to the knapsack.
